sourceBasis: Lesson titles and outcomes: docs/finance-modules/blueprint.json (travel-money entries).

es-en_regional_terms: cuenta (bill) and factura: Spain usage is used in restaurant and hotel bills; Latin American usage may differ.
billete vs boleto for ticket; recibo vs comprobante for proof of payment (comprobante is used in Latin America).
datáfono and terminal are both used for the card reader; check the chosen form per region.
aparcamiento vs estacionamiento; taquilla vs boletería.
zumo vs jugo; autobús vs bus/camión; menú del día (Spain).
ayuntamiento and tasa local appear as generic local-government terms; check that no region-specific tax name is asserted as universal.
es-en_grammar: Tú and usted are mixed deliberately by scene (friends use tú, service uses usted); confirm the register choices are consistent in lesson 28 and Master 19.
Subjunctive usage in Core 12, Core 23, Master 6, Master 7, Master 10 and Master 20 should be reviewed for naturalness.
Pesar used figuratively in Core 3 and the pluperfect subjunctive in Master 5 are advanced; check the notes.
en-es_regional_terms: bill vs check for restaurant bills; pants vs trousers; subway vs metro vs tube; ATM vs cash machine.
pound used as a weight unit at markets (Foundation/Core); pound is also the currency; the Spanish glosses say libra for weight. Check the lessons where both senses could appear.
tap card and contactless are used generically; check the usage note for each region.
en-es_grammar: Phrasal verbs (check out, pick up, split, run out) are used and glossed; check the Spanish gloss wording.
Would have, had known and reported speech in Master 5, Master 9 and Master 10 are advanced; check the Spanish explanation.
Some English verb notes use the form is irregular; these are checked only by the author-side validator, not by a linguist.
jurisdiction: Tax and local-charge labels are described generically (tasa local, impuesto local, cargo de servicio, service charge). No universal tax, deposit-protection or retirement claims are made.
Deposits and holds are described as bank practice in general terms; the release timing is a fictional example and not a legal rule.

knownGaps: No native-speaker review has been done for any lesson.
Regional terminology has not been verified against a regional glossary.
Learner-facing notes in es-en Foundation 1 and some Core notes are short; Opus may want to expand them.
Every Master speaking task includes a complication (verified in both files); Foundation and Core speaking tasks do not.
